messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Please help us test DataTables 1.10.2
parts:
Hi,

We just integrated the new version of the DataTables library (1.10.2)
into the development version of shiny. Due to the tremendous changes
in parameter names from DataTables 1.9.x to 1.10.x, we want to make
sure DataTables 1.10.2 still works reasonably well in shiny. If you
are interested in testing the development version, please install it
via:

if (!require("devtools")) install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github(c("rstudio/htmltools", "rstudio/shiny"))

A guide for upgrading parameter names from DT 1.9.x to 1.10.x is here:
https://datatables.net/upgrade/1.10-convert We have tried to
automatically correct some of the old parameter names in shiny, but
this automatic correction certainly won't work for all use cases,
especially if you have deeply customized your DataTables using
complicated JavaScript options. You can see
https://github.com/rstudio/shiny-examples/commit/6f2a5618 for examples
of converting DT 1.9 names to 1.10 names.

Please let us know if you have any comments or questions. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: Please help us test DataTables 1.10.2
parts:
Hi, 

Thanks for the dataTable update!

However, I also have som width issues in wide dataTables 1.10.
Example in a 21 column table fus(): 

  output$allfusions <- renderDataTable({
    fus.all()
  }, options = list(
    "orderClasses" = TRUE,
    "responsive" = TRUE,
    "pageLength" = 25),
    "escape" = FALSE
  )


In HTML it seems to attain a fixed width (3694px), then divided evenly among columns (291-292px).
 
<table class="table table-striped table-hover dataTable collapsed dtr-inline" id="DataTables_Table_0" role="grid" aria-describedby="DataTables_Table_0_info" style="width: 3694px;">
<thead>
  <tr role="row">
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="Tags: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 291px;">Tags</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="Count: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 291px;">Count</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="Sample: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 292px;">Sample</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="Subgroup: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 292px;">Subgroup</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="5end_GeneSymbol: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 292px;">5end_GeneSymbol</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="3end_GeneSymbol: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 292px;">3end_GeneSymbol</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="Fusion_point_5end: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 292px;">Fusion_point_5end</th>
    <th class="sorting" tabindex="0" aria-controls="DataTables_Table_0" rowspan="1" colspan="1" aria-label="Fusion_point_3end: activate to sort column ascending" style="width: 292px;">Fusion_point_3end</th>

...

Is this the expected behaviour?
Wrapping the table in column() or some div with max-width does not seem to help either. 

Note that I'm here using the "responsive" option (with inclusion of dataTables.responsive.js), but that it fails to break the table at the right point - very likely due to this same issue. 
Not using "responsive" produces identical results. 

/Vasilios

parts:
Sorry, this is actually an issue introduced by activating the responsive extension. 
(This does not happen with responsive dataTables outside Shiny though)

Inactive, the width of the table is the same (3694px) - but the column widths are relative to their content instead.
I will look into the js/css added for responsive to try and understand where the conflict might be. 
In any case, supporting the responsive option would be very useful in Shiny as I often find myself wanting to display tables > 5-10 columns. 

/Vasilios
